summary.headline: A debt-free, high-return supplier to its parent, priced about right
summary.text: ACL Plastics PLC (APLA.N0000) makes the PVC compound that coats cables, and sells about 97% of it to its parent ACL Cables and sister company Kelani Cables. It is a small, debt-free and very profitable business: return on equity was 20% in the year to March 2026 and has averaged about 22% over five years, and about a third of its value is cash and unit trusts (Rs 2.2bn net, about Rs 52 a share). Profit for the six months to September 2026 rose 28% (EPS Rs 10.72), though the September quarter was 10% lower as margins narrowed. At Rs 159 (30 September close; check the live price) the share trades at 7.5x trailing earnings and 1.4x its NAV of Rs 111.51. The methods put fair value at about Rs 139, so the price is about 14% above it: fairly priced rather than cheap. I'd buy at up to about Rs 118 and treat under Rs 104 as a strong buy.

fullText:
Summary: ACL Plastics PLC (APLA.N0000) makes the PVC compound that coats cables, and sells about 97% of it to its parent ACL Cables and sister company Kelani Cables. It is a small, debt-free and very profitable business: return on equity was 20% in the year to March 2026 and has averaged about 22% over five years, and about a third of its value is cash and unit trusts (Rs 2.2bn net, about Rs 52 a share). Profit for the six months to September 2026 rose 28% (EPS Rs 10.72), though the September quarter was 10% lower as margins narrowed. At Rs 159 (30 September close; check the live price) the share trades at 7.5x trailing earnings and 1.4x its NAV of Rs 111.51. The methods put fair value at about Rs 139, so the price is about 14% above it: fairly priced rather than cheap. I'd buy at up to about Rs 118 and treat under Rs 104 as a strong buy.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 159.00 (closing price 30 September 2026, from the interim report). Please check it live. In July–September 2026 it traded between Rs 135 and Rs 172. It closed March 2026 at Rs 131.25.
Six months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited): revenue Rs 1.53bn (up 16%), profit Rs 452mn (up 28%), EPS Rs 10.72 (Rs 8.37). The September quarter: revenue Rs 788mn (up 28%), gross margin 25% (31%), profit Rs 157mn (down 10%), EPS Rs 3.73.
Year to March 2026 (audited): revenue Rs 2.85bn (up 17%), gross margin 31% (24%), profit Rs 798mn (up 72%), EPS Rs 18.94 (Rs 11.03), ROE 20%. Trailing EPS is about Rs 21.29.
NAV Rs 111.51 a share (September 2026). 42.1 million shares after the 1-for-10 split. ACL Cables owns 65%.

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Justified P/B | 65.0 | 117.1 | 195.1 | 117.1
Business at a P/E plus cash | 109.5 | 161.3 | 220.9 | 157.7
Residual income | 68.5 | 133.4 | 271.6 | 141.6
Average | 81.0 | 137.3 | 229.2 | 138.8
Fair value about Rs 139 (30% bear, 50% base, 20% bull). Buy at up to Rs 118 (15% below); strong buy under Rs 104 (25% below).

Assumptions
Cost of equity 18% / 16.5% / 15%, against government bonds of about 12%. Long-run ROE 13% / 17% / 21% (five-year average about 22%). Growth 6% / 6.5% / 7%. Operating business: profit after tax of Rs 9.10 / 13.30 / 16.60 a share at 6 / 8 / 10 times, plus Rs 54.90 of net cash and investments.

What stands out
- Debt-free with Rs 2.4bn of unit trusts, deposits and cash (Rs 221mn of short-term borrowing at September).
- Captive customers: 97% of sales to ACL Cables and Kelani Cables. This keeps volumes steady but means the group sets the margin.
- Some of the latest profit is market and currency gains (Rs 77mn unit trusts, Rs 66mn exchange in the half).
- Dividend raised to Rs 3.75 (from Rs 2.50), about 20% of profit.

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 139, 150 up to Rs 118, 150 up to Rs 104: average about Rs 122, about Rs 61,100 in total. Rs 118 needs about a 26% fall; the share was Rs 131 in March 2026, so that's within reach in a market dip.

What would change my view
Higher: strong cable demand at ACL and Kelani, gross margin back above 30%, a bigger or special dividend, customers outside the group.
Lower: the group squeezing margins, PVC resin costs rising, a cable slowdown, the cash being used on poor terms within the group.

Business tests: 4 of 4 passed, so it's a good business priced a little above fair value: watch list.
